findings.title: Client-side rendering gap: raw HTML contains minimal text content
findings.evidence: Observed at https://yandex.com/ via static_initial_html_shell_inspection [2026-09-13T16:00:26Z]: Raw HTML yields only 21 words of visible text and shows static shell signals (many-inline-or-external-scripts, markup-to-text-imbalance). Search crawlers and AI bots that do not execute client JS may not extract brand facts from this page. Other page-level checks were suppressed here: a missing heading, CTA, meta description or schema on an empty shell are all symptoms of this one root cause. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Implement server-side rendering (SSR) or static pre-rendering for core content.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Use static site generation (SSG) or SSR so that primary textual facts and headers are present in initial HTTP responses without JS execution.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves render gap by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

findings.title: Brand identity is not anchored to any independent authority source
findings.evidence: Observed at https://yandex.com via onsite_identity_anchor_inspection [2026-09-13T16:00:42Z]: Across the crawled pages, no Organization schema is present, so no sameAs URIs can be declared, and 0 of 7 distinct outbound link domains point to an independent authority (Wikipedia, Wikidata, Crunchbase, LinkedIn, GitHub, regulatory registries). No explicit independent-authority link was observed in the sampled pages; external corroboration was not searched. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Publish machine-readable identity anchors linking the brand to independent authorities.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add Organization JSON-LD with a stable @id, legalName, and a sameAs array pointing to the brand's Wikidata item, Wikipedia article, LinkedIn company page and Crunchbase profile. Create those external profiles first if they do not exist -- sameAs pointing at nothing does not corroborate anything.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves corroboration by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

findings.title: Content images carry no text alternative, hiding any fact they display
findings.evidence: Observed at https://yandex.com/support/adfox/en/ via image_alt_coverage_inspection [2026-09-13T16:00:26Z]: 10 of 12 images (83%) have no alt attribute at all (images correctly marked decorative with alt="" are excluded). Any figure, price, spec or claim rendered inside those images is unreadable to a retrieval bot. (Confidence: high)

suggested_action.summary: Add descriptive alt text to every image that carries information.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Give each informational image an alt attribute stating the fact it conveys ("Pro plan: $49 per user per month"), not a filename. Mark purely decorative images with alt="" so they are correctly skipped rather than left unlabelled.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves fact extractability by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

evidence_details.observation: 10 of 12 images (83%) have no alt attribute at all (images correctly marked decorative with alt="" are excluded). Any figure, price, spec or claim rendered inside those images is unreadable to a retrieval bot.

findings.severity_rationale: Rated low because the observed evidence indicates low impact; unavailable evidence is not treated as a defect.

findings.title: No returning-visitor or account affordance detected
findings.evidence: Observed at https://yandex.com via returning_visitor_affordance_detection [2026-09-13T16:00:26Z]: Across 2 crawled pages there is no sign-in, account, saved-items or recently-viewed affordance in the visible text. Every visitor is therefore treated as anonymous and first-time, so nothing the brand already knows about a returning visitor can shape what they are shown. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Give returning visitors a way to be recognised, and use it.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add an account or saved-state affordance appropriate to the site (sign-in, saved items, recently viewed, or a lightweight preference stored locally), then use it to surface relevant content on return rather than resetting every visitor to a cold start.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves personalization readiness by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

findings.title: No extractable answer on-site for "What makes Yandex different?"
findings.evidence: Observed at https://yandex.com/ via onsite_answerability_probe [2026-09-13T16:00:42Z]: Across 2 crawled page(s), no explicit differentiator or benefit statement is extractable from the relevant crawled pages. An assistant that fetched these pages could not quote an answer to "What makes Yandex different?" from this site, so it must fall back to third-party sources or omit the brand. (Confidence: medium)

suggested_action.summary: Make the brand's differentiator explicit and quotable.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add a short, factual differentiator section tied to a specific capability, audience, outcome, or proof point.
suggested_action.expected_benefit: Improves citation omission by making the observed information clearer and more extractable for the intended audience.

proactive_recommendations.title: Build third-party presence so Yandex is resolvable away from its own domain
proactive_recommendations.rationale: Only 0 independent authority domain(s) are referenced from the crawled pages. Assistants weight facts that several unrelated sources agree on, and the major platforms draw on largely different source pools -- analyses of 2026 citation data find roughly 11% domain overlap between ChatGPT and Perplexity. A brand described only on its own site is a single fragile source no matter how well that site is built.

suggested_action.summary: Establish and maintain the brand on independent platforms, then link them via sameAs.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Create or claim a Wikidata item, a LinkedIn company page, and the profiles that matter in your sector (Crunchbase, GitHub, G2, industry registries). Keep the core facts identical across them, then reference them from Organization sameAs so the identity is machine-linkable.

proactive_recommendations.title: Add Article schema with author and dateModified to editorial pages
proactive_recommendations.rationale: 1 crawled page(s) are editorial or documentation content carrying no Article schema. Authorship and a machine-readable modification date are the signals assistants use to decide whether a passage is current and attributable -- without them, an assistant that finds a good answer on the page still has no basis to date it or credit it.

suggested_action.summary: Mark editorial and documentation pages with Article JSON-LD.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add Article or TechArticle JSON-LD with headline, author (a Person or Organization with a real profile URL), datePublished and dateModified. Update dateModified when the content genuinely changes, not on every deploy.

proactive_recommendations.title: Declare a WebSite entity with SearchAction
proactive_recommendations.rationale: No WebSite schema was found. WebSite ties the domain to the brand entity and, with a potentialAction SearchAction, lets assistants point users straight into your own search instead of guessing at URLs. It is a small, stable addition that anchors everything else on the page to a named site.

suggested_action.summary: Add WebSite JSON-LD with a SearchAction pointing at your search endpoint.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add WebSite JSON-LD on the homepage with name, url, a publisher reference to your Organization @id, and potentialAction -> SearchAction with a target URL template.

proactive_recommendations.title: Add BreadcrumbList schema to deep pages
proactive_recommendations.rationale: 1 crawled page(s) sit two or more levels deep with no BreadcrumbList markup. Breadcrumbs give both a visitor arriving cold from an AI answer and the assistant itself the parent context a deep URL otherwise lacks.

suggested_action.summary: Add BreadcrumbList JSON-LD alongside visible breadcrumb navigation.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Emit BreadcrumbList JSON-LD listing each ancestor with position, name and item URL, and render the same trail visibly at the top of the page.

proactive_recommendations.title: State AI usage terms explicitly in robots.txt
proactive_recommendations.rationale: robots.txt names which agents may crawl but says nothing about what may be done with the content once fetched. Emerging conventions -- Cloudflare's Content Signals Policy (released CC0) and RSL licensing terms -- let a publisher separate training use from search indexing and answer generation in machine-readable form, instead of leaving that distinction to be inferred from which user agents happen to be listed.

suggested_action.summary: Add machine-readable content-usage signals to robots.txt.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: Add a Content Signals Policy block declaring your position on search, ai-input and ai-train separately, or publish RSL licensing terms. Keep it consistent with the agents you actually allow, or the two signals will contradict each other.

proactive_recommendations.title: Consider publishing llms.txt, with realistic expectations
proactive_recommendations.rationale: No /llms.txt is published. Be aware this is a low-evidence convention rather than an established standard: 2026 measurements find major AI crawlers almost never request the file, and Google has stated it has no effect on Search or AI Overviews. It costs very little to publish and may matter if uptake improves, but it should be treated as optionality -- not as a substitute for the structured data and third-party presence that demonstrably drive citation today.

suggested_action.summary: Optionally publish /llms.txt, after the higher-leverage items above.
suggested_action.how_to_fix: If you publish one, keep it to a short markdown index of your canonical product, docs, pricing and company pages, and keep it in sync with the site. Do not deprioritise schema work for it.
